description: Political meme contrasting the years in government of six Democratic politicians (Joe Biden, Chuck Schumer, Nancy Pelosi, Patrick Leahy, Maxine Waters, Dianne Feinstein, with photos and claimed entry years) against Donald Trump, shown with the claim he entered politics in 2015 with 3 years in government. The red text argues these long-serving politicians are blaming Trump for problems they have not solved for decades. Some of the stated entry years/tenures are approximate or disputed.
text: JOE BIDEN. ENTERED POLITICS IN 1969. (51 YEARS IN GOVERNMENT). 51 YRS. CHUCK SCHUMER. ENTERED POLITICS IN 1975. (45 YEARS IN GOVERNMENT). 45 YRS. NANCY PELOSI. ENTERED POLITICS IN 1987. (33 YEARS IN GOVERNMENT). 33 YRS. PATRICK LEAHY. ENTERED POLITICS IN 1966. (54 YEARS IN GOVERNMENT). 54 YRS. MAXINE WATERS. ENTERED POLITICS IN 1973. (47 YEARS IN GOVERNMENT). 47 YRS. DIANNE FEINSTEIN. ENTERED POLITICS IN 1960. (60 YEARS IN GOVERNMENT). 60 YRS. ARE BLAMING THIS GUY. DONALD J TRUMP. ENTERED POLITICS IN 2015. (3 YEARS IN GOVERNMENT). FOR PROBLEMS THEY HAVEN'T SOLVED FOR DECADES.
flags: Entry-year and tenure figures are the meme's claims and are approximate/disputed in places (e.g. Feinstein 1960, Trump 3 years as of 2020)

description: Simple red-and-white graphic reading '73-0' in large white numerals with the caption 'President Trump's Perfect Congressional Endorsement Record'. A campaign-style stat card claiming candidates endorsed by Trump in congressional primaries had won 73 races and lost none as of June 2020.
text: 73-0. PRESIDENT TRUMP'S PERFECT CONGRESSIONAL ENDORSEMENT RECORD.
flags: The 73-0 endorsement tally is the graphic's claim; scope and count are unverified

description: Photograph of a veterans memorial display in a tree-lined park: hundreds of small white crosses bearing name placards and American flags planted in grass, with dozens of crosses knocked over and flags scattered on the ground, indicating the display was toppled or vandalized. The image circulated in June 2020 with claims that a Memorial Day cross display had been vandalized; the location is not identifiable from the image itself. Legible placards carry names of honored veterans.
text: CLYDE COLLINS COLE. RAYMOND CHANEY JR. WILBUR CHANEY.
flags: Location and cause of the toppled crosses are not shown in the image; vandalism claim comes from accompanying context (widely reported at the time as a Kentucky park memorial)
Names on the crosses are memorial placards for deceased veterans, transcribed only as visible text
